svg.text: Raspberry Pi 5 · HiLetgo TXS0108E level shifter · 176 × WS2812B (144 LED/m) · data on SPI0 MOSI = GPIO10, physical pin 19 (D-28)
WS2812B / SK6812 · 144 LED/m · 176 LEDs · 1222 mm · GRB · LED 0 sits at A0
data flows LED 0 → LED 175 — follow the arrows printed on the tape
stands in for D-11's 74AHCT125 — see note ③
pin 1 = inner row, end away from USB
never power the strip from the Pi
single ground tie: Pi ↔ LED PSU (the only one)
TXS VA, and TXS OE (OE low = outputs off)
R1 330 Ω → strip DIN at LED 0
TXS VB · strip +5 V at LED 0, 88, 175
one wire to the GND bus: the only tie point
+ to +5 V, − to GND, at injection #1
its own USB-C PD 5 V / 5 A, nothing else
• power the strip from the Pi's 5 V pins (2 / 4)
• power the Pi from the LED brick or from the strip's far end
• tie the Pi's ground to the LED ground at more than one point
③ TXS0108E instead of the 74AHCT125 the docs specify (D-11)
VA is the low side (3.3 V), VB the high side (5 V); VA must not exceed VB.
OE must be tied to VA, or every output stays high-impedance (nothing lights).
Outputs are weak, auto-direction one-shots: keep B1 → DIN short and add
no pull-up / pull-down resistors on A1 or B1.
If led_test.py 'first' shows garbage or flicker, suspect the TXS first:
shorten the B1 wire, then fall back to a 74AHCT125 (BOM item 7).
Clone pinouts vary: check the module's silkscreen against this drawing.
A hop (⌒) is a crossing with no connection; a dot is a junction.
Sources: docs/hardware.md §4.4, §4.5, §6.1a · docs/build.md step 3 · docs/decisions.md D-11, D-20, D-27, D-28
